#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# License: BSD-3 (https://tldrlegal.com/license/bsd-3-clause-license-(revised))
# Copyright (c) 2026, Rosenfeld, Hernán; Cabral, Juan B.
# All rights reserved.

# =============================================================================
# DOCS
# =============================================================================

"""Plotting accessor for :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instances \
(``volcano.plot``)."""

# =============================================================================
# IMPORTS
# =============================================================================

import matplotlib.colors as mcolors
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import MaxNLocator

import numpy as np

import pandas as pd

from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde

import seaborn as sns

from .base import AccessorABC
from ..constants import (
    DIRECTION_ORDER,
    METERS_PER_DEGREE,
    NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS as _NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS,
)

# =============================================================================
# FUNCTIONS
# =============================================================================


def _polar_axes(ax):
    """Return ``ax`` if it's polar (new polar axes if None), else raise."""
    if ax is None:
        return plt.subplot(projection="polar")
    if ax.name != "polar":
        raise ValueError(
            "'ax' must be a polar axes (projection='polar'), "
            f"found {ax.name!r}"
        )
    return ax


def _draw_grid(ax, row, title, label, colorbar, **kwargs):
    """Draw a scene-shaped row (``(direction, distance)`` index) as an image.

    The row's index must run direction-major in
    :data:`~volcanicus.constants.DIRECTION_ORDER`, as the columns of
    :meth:`~volcanicus.accessors.scenes.ScenesAccessor.grid` do, so it reshapes
    straight into the (direction, distance) grid.
    """
    distances = list(row.index.unique("distance"))
    grid = row.to_numpy(dtype=float).reshape(
        len(DIRECTION_ORDER), len(distances)
    )

    kwargs.setdefault("aspect", "auto")
    ax = plt.gca() if ax is None else ax
    image = ax.imshow(grid, **kwargs)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(DIRECTION_ORDER)), DIRECTION_ORDER)
    step = max(1, len(distances) // 6)
    ax.set_xticks(range(0, len(distances), step), distances[::step])
    ax.set_xlabel("Distance")
    ax.set_ylabel("Direction")
    ax.set_title(title)
    if colorbar:
        ax.figure.colorbar(image, ax=ax, label=label)
    return ax


def _as_compass(ax):
    """Lay out polar axes as a compass: north up, clockwise, labeled."""
    ax.set_theta_zero_location("N")
    ax.set_theta_direction(-1)  # clockwise, like a compass
    bearings = np.radians(45.0 * np.arange(len(DIRECTION_ORDER)))
    ax.set_xticks(bearings, DIRECTION_ORDER)


# =============================================================================
# CLASSES
# =============================================================================


class PlotAccessor(AccessorABC):
    """Plotting accessor for a :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instance \
    (used as ``volcano.plot``).

    Instances are callable: ``volcano.plot(kind, **kwargs)`` dispatches to
    the method named ``kind`` (``"radial_profile"`` by default, see
    :attr:`_default_kind`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    volcano : Volcano
        The :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instance this accessor belongs
        to.

    """

    _default_kind = "radial_profile"

    def __init__(self, volcano):
        self._volcano = volcano

    def radial_profile(
        self,
        ax=None,
        direction_kwds=None,
        median_kwds=None,
        directions=True,
        median=True,
        std=False,
    ):
        """Plot residual values against distance, one line per direction.

        There are two underlying seaborn plots: one line per direction, and
        (optionally) one aggregate line summarizing all directions. Since
        there are only 8 directions, that aggregate uses the median rather
        than the mean, to be less sensitive to any single outlying
        direction. To keep the plot simple and easy to read at a glance, the
        median line never shows error bars — only ``std`` for the
        per-direction lines is configurable. Instead of hard-coding their
        keyword arguments, ``direction_kwds`` and ``median_kwds`` let the
        caller override or extend what each ``sns.lineplot`` call receives;
        anything not explicitly provided falls back to this method's own
        defaults (``errorbar="sd"``/``err_style="bars"`` for the
        per-direction plot with ``hue="direction"``, and
        ``color="black"``/``estimator="median"``/``label="Median"`` for the
        aggregate plot).

        Uses the raw (non-averaged) measurements so seaborn can compute, for
        every direction, error bars across dates at each distance bin — not
        just for the overall mean.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            Axes to draw on. A new figure and axes are created if not given.
        direction_kwds : dict, optional
            Keyword arguments forwarded to the per-direction ``sns.lineplot``
            call, on top of this method's own defaults.
        median_kwds : dict, optional
            Keyword arguments forwarded to the aggregate ``sns.lineplot``
            call, on top of this method's own defaults.
        directions : bool, default True
            Whether to draw the per-direction lines at all — turn this off
            (with ``median=True``) to get just the aggregate line, e.g. to
            overlay several volcanoes' median curves on the same axes for
            comparison. This is a plotting-only switch: it has no
            equivalent on :meth:`Volcano.radial_profile`.
        median : bool, default True
            Whether to draw the aggregate (median) line at all.
        std : bool, default False
            Whether error bars are shown on the per-direction lines (the
            median line never shows error bars); ignored if ``errorbar`` is
            set explicitly via ``direction_kwds``.

        Returns
        -------
        matplotlib.axes.Axes
            The axes the plot was drawn on.

        """
        # Fill in this method's own defaults for whatever the caller didn't
        # already set explicitly via direction_kwds/median_kwds.
        direction_kwds = {} if direction_kwds is None else direction_kwds
        direction_kwds.setdefault("alpha", 0.5 if median else 1)
        direction_kwds.setdefault("hue", "direction")
        direction_kwds.setdefault("errorbar", "sd" if std else None)
        direction_kwds.setdefault("err_style", "bars")

        median_kwds = {} if median_kwds is None else median_kwds
        median_kwds.setdefault("color", "black")
        median_kwds.setdefault("linewidth", 2)
        median_kwds.setdefault("errorbar", None)
        median_kwds.setdefault("estimator", "median")
        median_kwds.setdefault("label", "Median")

        ax = plt.gca() if ax is None else ax

        if directions:
            # Layer 1 (optional): one line per direction. Reshape from
            # one-column-per-distance-bin (wide) to one row per (direction,
            # distance, residual) observation (long), which is what
            # seaborn's lineplot expects for it to compute per-direction
            # error bars across the repeated (raw, non-averaged)
            # observations.
            df = self._volcano.to_dataframe()
            distance_columns = [
                c for c in df.columns if c not in _NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS
            ]
            long_df = df.melt(
                id_vars="direction",
                value_vars=distance_columns,
                var_name="distance",
                value_name="residual",
            )
            sns.lineplot(
                data=long_df,
                x="distance",
                y="residual",
                ax=ax,
                **direction_kwds,
            )

        if median:
            # Layer 2 (optional): a single aggregate line summarizing all
            # directions. Volcano.radial_profile() already reduces to one
            # row per direction; the median line's errorbar then reflects
            # spread *between directions*, not between raw dates. Median
            # (not mean) because there are only 8 directions, so it's more
            # robust to any single outlying direction.
            by_direction = self._volcano.radial_profile().reset_index()
            median_long_df = by_direction.melt(
                id_vars="direction", var_name="distance", value_name="residual"
            )
            sns.lineplot(
                data=median_long_df,
                x="distance",
                y="residual",
                ax=ax,
                **median_kwds,
            )

        ax.set_xlabel("Distance (m)")
        ax.set_ylabel("Residual")
        ax.set_title(
            f"{self._volcano.name}: residual vs. distance by direction"
        )
        ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
        return ax

    def temporal_profile(
        self,
        ax=None,
        direction_kwds=None,
        median_kwds=None,
        directions=True,
        median=True,
        std=False,
    ):
        """Plot residual values against date, one line per direction.

        Temporal mirror of :meth:`radial_profile`: same two-layer plot (one
        line per direction, plus an optional aggregate median line), but
        with ``date`` on the x-axis. Error bars on the per-direction lines
        are computed across distance bins (repeated observations at each
        date), instead of across dates.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            Axes to draw on. A new figure and axes are created if not given.
        direction_kwds : dict, optional
            Keyword arguments forwarded to the per-direction ``sns.lineplot``
            call, on top of this method's own defaults.
        median_kwds : dict, optional
            Keyword arguments forwarded to the aggregate ``sns.lineplot``
            call, on top of this method's own defaults.
        directions : bool, default True
            Whether to draw the per-direction lines at all — turn this off
            (with ``median=True``) to get just the aggregate line, e.g. to
            overlay several volcanoes' median curves on the same axes for
            comparison. This is a plotting-only switch: it has no
            equivalent on :meth:`Volcano.temporal_profile`.
        median : bool, default True
            Whether to draw the aggregate (median) line at all.
        std : bool, default False
            Whether error bars are shown on the per-direction lines (the
            median line never shows error bars); ignored if ``errorbar`` is
            set explicitly via ``direction_kwds``.

        Returns
        -------
        matplotlib.axes.Axes
            The axes the plot was drawn on.

        """
        # Fill in this method's own defaults for whatever the caller didn't
        # already set explicitly via direction_kwds/median_kwds.
        direction_kwds = {} if direction_kwds is None else direction_kwds
        direction_kwds.setdefault("alpha", 0.5 if median else 1)
        direction_kwds.setdefault("hue", "direction")
        direction_kwds.setdefault("errorbar", "sd" if std else None)
        direction_kwds.setdefault("err_style", "bars")

        median_kwds = {} if median_kwds is None else median_kwds
        median_kwds.setdefault("color", "black")
        median_kwds.setdefault("linewidth", 2)
        median_kwds.setdefault("errorbar", None)
        median_kwds.setdefault("estimator", "median")
        median_kwds.setdefault("label", "Median")

        ax = plt.gca() if ax is None else ax

        if directions:
            # Layer 1 (optional): one line per direction. Reshape from
            # one-column-per-distance-bin (wide) to one row per (date,
            # direction, distance, residual) observation (long); this time
            # keeping date/direction so seaborn can compute, per direction
            # and date, error bars across the repeated distance-bin
            # observations (the temporal mirror of radial_profile's melt).
            df = self._volcano.to_dataframe()
            distance_columns = [
                c for c in df.columns if c not in _NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS
            ]
            long_df = df.melt(
                id_vars=["date", "direction"],
                value_vars=distance_columns,
                var_name="distance",
                value_name="residual",
            )
            sns.lineplot(
                data=long_df, x="date", y="residual", ax=ax, **direction_kwds
            )

        if median:
            # Layer 2 (optional): a single aggregate line summarizing all
            # directions. Volcano.temporal_profile() already reduces to one
            # row per date; the median line's errorbar then reflects spread
            # *between directions*, not between raw distance bins. Median
            # (not mean) because there are only 8 directions, so it's more
            # robust to any single outlying direction.
            by_date = self._volcano.temporal_profile().reset_index()
            median_long_df = by_date.melt(
                id_vars="date", var_name="direction", value_name="residual"
            )
            sns.lineplot(
                data=median_long_df,
                x="date",
                y="residual",
                ax=ax,
                **median_kwds,
            )

        ax.set_xlabel("Date")
        ax.set_ylabel("Residual")
        ax.set_title(f"{self._volcano.name}: residual vs. date by direction")
        ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
        return ax

    def polar(
        self, ax=None, dates=None, cmap="viridis", colorbar=True, **kwargs
    ):
        """Plot every date as a polygon on a compass, colored by date.

        Each date becomes a closed polygon with one vertex per direction:
        the vertex's angle is the direction's compass bearing (north up,
        clockwise) and its radius the residual of that date/direction
        averaged over every distance bin (:meth:`Volcano.temporal_profile`).
        A round polygon means the residual is even around the vent; a
        lopsided one points towards where it's higher.

        Residuals can be negative, so the radial axis starts at the lowest
        value instead of 0; a dashed circle marks the zero residual. A
        direction missing on a date leaves a gap in that date's polygon.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            Polar axes to draw on (``projection="polar"``). New ones are
            created if not given.
        dates : list-like, optional
            Dates to plot. Defaults to every date.
        cmap : str or matplotlib.colors.Colormap, default "viridis"
            Colormap mapping each polygon's date to its color.
        colorbar : bool, default True
            Whether to add a colorbar labeling the dates.
        **kwargs
            Forwarded to every polygon's ``ax.plot`` call, on top of this
            method's defaults (``linewidth=1``, ``alpha=0.6``).

        Returns
        -------
        matplotlib.axes.Axes
            The axes the plot was drawn on.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``ax`` is not a polar axes.

        """
        kwargs.setdefault("linewidth", 1)
        kwargs.setdefault("alpha", 0.6)

        ax = _polar_axes(ax)

        # One row per date, one column per direction, in compass order (the
        # pivot inside temporal_profile sorts them alphabetically).
        profile = self._volcano.temporal_profile().reindex(
            columns=list(DIRECTION_ORDER)
        )
        if dates is not None:
            profile = profile.loc[pd.to_datetime(dates)]

        # Repeat the first direction at the end so every polygon closes.
        bearings = np.radians(45.0 * np.arange(len(DIRECTION_ORDER) + 1))
        closed = np.column_stack([profile, profile.iloc[:, 0]])

        cmap = plt.get_cmap(cmap)
        when = mdates.date2num(profile.index)
        norm = mcolors.Normalize(when.min(), when.max())
        for date_num, radii in zip(when, closed):
            ax.plot(bearings, radii, color=cmap(norm(date_num)), **kwargs)

        # Zero residual as a reference: the radial axis starts at the
        # lowest residual, so the center isn't 0.
        full_circle = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 100)
        ax.plot(full_circle, np.zeros_like(full_circle), "k--", linewidth=1)

        _as_compass(ax)
        ax.set_title(f"{self._volcano.name}: residual by direction and date")

        if colorbar:
            mappable = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(norm=norm, cmap=cmap)
            cbar = ax.figure.colorbar(mappable, ax=ax, pad=0.1)
            # Concise labels adapt to the span: years for decades of
            # data, months/days for a handful of nearby dates.
            locator = mdates.AutoDateLocator()
            cbar.ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(locator)
            cbar.ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
                mdates.ConciseDateFormatter(locator)
            )
            cbar.set_label("Date")
        return ax

    def scene(self, date, anomaly=False, ax=None, colorbar=True, **kwargs):
        """Plot one scene as an image: directions x distance bins.

        Every row is a direction (in
        :data:`~volcanicus.constants.DIRECTION_ORDER`) and every column a
        distance bin, colored by the residual
        (:meth:`ScenesAccessor.grid`) or, with ``anomaly=True``, by its
        z-score against the volcano's baseline
        (:meth:`AnomaliesAccessor.zscores`). Missing cells stay blank.

        Parameters
        ----------
        date : str or datetime-like
            Date of the scene to plot.
        anomaly : bool, default False
            Whether to plot anomalies instead of raw residuals. They get a
            diverging colormap (``"RdBu_r"``) centered on 0, so red is
            hotter than usual and blue colder. The color range is
            symmetric and clipped at the 95th percentile of ``|z|`` (at
            least 3), so a few extreme cells don't wash out the rest.
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            Axes to draw on. A new figure and axes are created if not given.
        colorbar : bool, default True
            Whether to add a colorbar.
        **kwargs
            Forwarded to ``ax.imshow``, on top of this method's defaults
            (``aspect="auto"``; for anomalies also ``cmap="RdBu_r"`` and
            ``vmin``/``vmax`` symmetric around 0).

        Returns
        -------
        matplotlib.axes.Axes
            The axes the plot was drawn on.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If the volcano has no scene on ``date``.

        """
        date = pd.Timestamp(date)
        scenes = (
            self._volcano.anomalies.zscores()
            if anomaly
            else self._volcano.scenes.grid()
        )
        if date not in scenes.index:
            raise KeyError(f"No scene on {date:%Y-%m-%d}")

        row = scenes.loc[date]
        if anomaly:
            # Symmetric limits keep 0 (the usual value) at the neutral
            # color of the diverging map; the floor of 3 keeps an ordinary
            # scene from looking alarming.
            values = row.to_numpy(dtype=float)
            finite = np.abs(values[np.isfinite(values)])
            limit = max(3.0, np.percentile(finite, 95)) if finite.size else 3.0
            kwargs.setdefault("cmap", "RdBu_r")
            kwargs.setdefault("vmin", -limit)
            kwargs.setdefault("vmax", limit)

        what = "anomaly (z)" if anomaly else "residual"
        return _draw_grid(
            ax,
            row,
            f"{self._volcano.name}: {what} on {date:%Y-%m-%d}",
            what.capitalize(),
            colorbar,
            **kwargs,
        )

    def baseline(
        self, stat="center", min_scenes=10, ax=None, colorbar=True, **kwargs
    ):
        """Plot the volcano's baseline as a directions x distance image.

        Same layout as :meth:`scene`, for one of the two rows of
        :meth:`AnomaliesAccessor.baseline`: every cell's usual value
        (``"center"``, the median over every scene) or its usual spread
        (``"scale"``, ``1.4826 * MAD``). Cells without a baseline (too few
        scenes, or never varying) stay blank.

        Parameters
        ----------
        stat : {"center", "scale"}, default "center"
            Which row of the baseline to plot.
        min_scenes : int, default 10
            Passed on to :meth:`AnomaliesAccessor.baseline`.
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            Axes to draw on. A new figure and axes are created if not given.
        colorbar : bool, default True
            Whether to add a colorbar.
        **kwargs
            Forwarded to ``ax.imshow``, on top of ``aspect="auto"``.

        Returns
        -------
        matplotlib.axes.Axes
            The axes the plot was drawn on.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``stat`` is not ``"center"`` or ``"scale"``.

        """
        labels = {"center": "Center (median)", "scale": "Scale (1.4826 x MAD)"}
        if stat not in labels:
            raise ValueError(
                f"'stat' must be one of {tuple(labels)}, found {stat!r}"
            )
        row = self._volcano.anomalies.baseline(min_scenes).loc[stat]
        return _draw_grid(
            ax,
            row,
            f"{self._volcano.name}: baseline {stat}",
            labels[stat],
            colorbar,
            **kwargs,
        )

    def episodes(
        self,
        threshold=3.0,
        max_gap=90,
        how="median",
        min_scenes=10,
        min_episode_scenes=1,
        ax=None,
    ):
        """Plot the anomaly score over time, with the episodes shaded.

        Draws :meth:`EpisodesAccessor.score`, a dashed line at
        ``threshold`` and a shaded band over every episode
        (:meth:`EpisodesAccessor.find`). A single-scene episode has no
        duration, so its band is widened to 16 days (one satellite
        revisit) to stay visible.

        Parameters
        ----------
        threshold, max_gap, how, min_scenes
            Passed on to :meth:`EpisodesAccessor.find`.
        min_episode_scenes : int, default 1
            Only shade episodes with at least this many scenes. Single-scene
            episodes are mostly chance crossings of the threshold, so ``2``
            is a sensible choice to show only the solid ones.
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            Axes to draw on. A new figure and axes are created if not given.

        Returns
        -------
        matplotlib.axes.Axes
            The axes the plot was drawn on.

        """
        score = self._volcano.episodes.score(how, min_scenes)
        episodes = self._volcano.episodes.find(
            threshold, max_gap, how, min_scenes
        )
        episodes = episodes[episodes["n_scenes"] >= min_episode_scenes]

        ax = plt.gca() if ax is None else ax
        score.plot(ax=ax, marker=".", linewidth=0.5, color="gray")
        ax.axhline(
            threshold,
            color="red",
            linestyle="--",
            linewidth=1,
            label="Threshold",
        )
        # One revisit as a minimum width, so single scenes show up.
        min_width = np.timedelta64(16, "D")
        for i, episode in enumerate(episodes.itertuples()):
            ax.axvspan(
                episode.start,
                max(episode.end, episode.start + min_width),
                color="orange",
                alpha=0.4,
                label="Episode" if i == 0 else None,
            )

        ax.set_xlabel("Date")
        ax.set_ylabel("Anomaly score")
        ax.set_title(f"{self._volcano.name}: anomaly score and episodes")
        ax.legend()
        return ax

    def azimuth_rose(self, bins=16, weighted=True, ax=None, **kwargs):
        """Plot where the heat points, over every scene, as a compass rose.

        A histogram of the scenes' ``azimuth``
        (:meth:`DescriptorsAccessor.table`) on a compass (north up,
        clockwise). By default every scene is weighted by its
        ``anisotropy``, so scenes where the heat is spread evenly (and the
        azimuth means little) barely count, and the rose shows where the
        heat goes when one side dominates. Scenes without an azimuth are
        left out.

        Parameters
        ----------
        bins : int, default 16
            Number of sectors, centered on the bearings: with 16, every
            sector spans 22.5° and the 8 compass directions fall at the
            center of every other one.
        weighted : bool, default True
            Whether to weight every scene by its ``anisotropy``. If False,
            the rose just counts scenes.
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            Polar axes to draw on (``projection="polar"``). New ones are
            created if not given.
        **kwargs
            Forwarded to ``ax.bar``.

        Returns
        -------
        matplotlib.axes.Axes
            The axes the plot was drawn on.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``ax`` is not a polar axes.

        """
        ax = _polar_axes(ax)
        descriptors = self._volcano.descriptors.table().dropna(
            subset=["azimuth"]
        )

        # Shift by half a sector so sectors are centered on the bearings
        # (e.g. N spans -11.25° to 11.25° with 16 bins).
        width = 360.0 / bins
        shifted = (descriptors["azimuth"] + width / 2) % 360
        weights = descriptors["anisotropy"] if weighted else None
        counts, edges = np.histogram(
            shifted, bins=bins, range=(0, 360), weights=weights
        )

        ax.bar(
            np.radians(edges[:-1]), counts, width=np.radians(width), **kwargs
        )
        _as_compass(ax)
        what = "anisotropy-weighted azimuth" if weighted else "azimuth"
        ax.set_title(f"{self._volcano.name}: {what}")
        return ax

    #: Reductions :meth:`rays_rose` accepts for its ``how`` parameter.
    _RAYS_ROSE_HOW = ("median", "mean", "max", "min")

    def rays_rose(self, column="peak", how="median", ax=None, **kwargs):
        """Plot a ray descriptor per direction, over every date, on a compass.

        One bar per direction, as long as ``column`` of
        :meth:`RaysAccessor.descriptors` reduced over every date with
        ``how``: with the defaults, the typical (median) peak of each
        direction, i.e. which side of the vent usually runs hotter. Unlike
        :meth:`azimuth_rose`, which shows where the heat goes when one side
        dominates, this shows the typical state of every direction.

        Parameters
        ----------
        column : str, default "peak"
            Ray descriptor to plot (a column of
            :meth:`RaysAccessor.descriptors`).
        how : str, default "median"
            Reduction over dates: ``"median"``, ``"mean"``, ``"max"`` or
            ``"min"``.
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            Polar axes to draw on (``projection="polar"``). New ones are
            created if not given.
        **kwargs
            Forwarded to ``ax.bar``, on top of this method's default
            ``width`` (40° per bar).

        Returns
        -------
        matplotlib.axes.Axes
            The axes the plot was drawn on.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``column`` is not a ray descriptor, ``how`` is not a
            supported reduction, or ``ax`` is not a polar axes.

        """
        rays = self._volcano.rays.descriptors()
        if column not in rays.columns:
            raise ValueError(
                f"'column' must be one of {tuple(rays.columns)}, "
                f"found {column!r}"
            )
        if how not in self._RAYS_ROSE_HOW:
            raise ValueError(
                f"'how' must be one of {self._RAYS_ROSE_HOW}, found {how!r}"
            )
        ax = _polar_axes(ax)

        by_direction = rays[column].groupby(level="direction", sort=False)
        values = getattr(by_direction, how)().reindex(DIRECTION_ORDER)

        kwargs.setdefault("width", np.radians(40))
        bearings = np.radians(45.0 * np.arange(len(DIRECTION_ORDER)))
        ax.bar(bearings, values.to_numpy(dtype=float), **kwargs)
        _as_compass(ax)
        ax.set_title(f"{self._volcano.name}: {how} ray {column} by direction")
        return ax

    #: Share of the centers the fill of :meth:`centers_map` covers.
    _CENTERS_MAP_SUPPORT = 0.95

    def centers_map(
        self,
        temperature="peak",
        fill=True,
        centers=True,
        spread=True,
        reference=True,
        cmap="hot",
        vmin=None,
        vmax=None,
        center=None,
        color="k",
        colorbar=True,
        legend=True,
        ax=None,
    ):
        """Map every date's center around their centroid, with its temperature.

        Every date has a center (``center_lat``/``center_long``), the focus
        the measurements are taken around. The map is a compass (north up,
        clockwise) whose origin is the centroid of every center: the angle
        is the bearing from it and the radius the distance, in meters.

        The background is the scenes' ``temperature``
        (:meth:`DescriptorsAccessor.table`) smoothed in space: every
        location gets the mean of the nearby centers, weighted by a Gaussian
        kernel as wide as a KDE of the centers (Scott's rule). It is only
        drawn over the densest region holding 95% of the centers, so it
        doesn't extrapolate where there are none. The fill and the spread
        ellipse are left out when the centers don't span a plane (fewer than
        three dates, or all of them on a line).

        Parameters
        ----------
        temperature : str, default "peak"
            Scene descriptor (a column of
            :meth:`DescriptorsAccessor.table`) that gives every center its
            temperature.
        fill : bool, default True
            Whether to color the background with the smoothed temperature.
        centers : bool, default True
            Whether to draw every center as a dot, colored by its
            temperature on the same scale as the fill: a dot standing out
            from its background is a scene hotter (or colder) than its
            neighbors.
        spread : bool, default True
            Whether to draw the dashed 1-sigma ellipse of the centers.
        reference : bool, default True
            Whether to mark the volcano's GVP location
            (:attr:`Volcano.gvp_lat`, :attr:`Volcano.gvp_lon`) with a star.
        cmap : str or matplotlib.colors.Colormap, default "hot"
            Colormap of the temperature. Values beyond ``vmin``/``vmax`` get
            the end colors.
        vmin, vmax : float, optional
            Temperatures at the ends of the colormap. Default to the 2nd and
            98th percentile of the temperature, so a few extreme scenes don't
            wash out the rest. Fix them (e.g. ``0`` and ``1`` for ``peak``)
            to compare several volcanoes on the same scale.
        center : float, optional
            Temperature at the middle of the colormap, as in
            :func:`seaborn.heatmap`: each half of the colormap stretches to
            cover its side, so the colors are no longer linear across
            ``center``. Must lie strictly between ``vmin`` and ``vmax``.
        color : color, default "k"
            Color of the spread ellipse and the GVP star.
        colorbar : bool, default True
            Whether to add a colorbar of the temperature.
        legend : bool, default True
            Whether to add a legend of the centers, ellipse and star.
        ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
            Polar axes to draw on (``projection="polar"``). New ones are
            created if not given.

        Returns
        -------
        matplotlib.axes.Axes
            The axes the plot was drawn on.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``ax`` is not a polar axes, or ``center`` is not strictly
            between ``vmin`` and ``vmax``.
        KeyError
            If ``temperature`` is not a scene descriptor.

        """
        ax = _polar_axes(ax)

        # One center per date (every direction of a date shares it), as
        # east/north offsets in meters from their centroid; a degree of
        # longitude shrinks with the cosine of the latitude.
        df = self._volcano.to_dataframe()
        by_date = df.groupby("date")[["center_lat", "center_long"]].first()
        lat0, lon0 = by_date.mean()

        def to_xy(lat, lon):
            north = (lat - lat0) * METERS_PER_DEGREE
            east = (lon - lon0) * METERS_PER_DEGREE * np.cos(np.radians(lat0))
            return np.asarray(east), np.asarray(north)

        def to_polar(east, north):
            # (east, north), not (north, east): bearings start at north
            # and grow towards east.
            return np.arctan2(east, north), np.hypot(east, north)

        points = np.vstack(
            to_xy(by_date["center_lat"], by_date["center_long"])
        )
        temp = (
            self._volcano.descriptors.table()[temperature]
            .reindex(by_date.index)
            .to_numpy(dtype=float)
        )
        low, high = np.nanpercentile(temp, [2, 98])
        vmin = low if vmin is None else vmin
        vmax = high if vmax is None else vmax
        norm = (
            mcolors.Normalize(vmin, vmax)
            if center is None
            else mcolors.TwoSlopeNorm(center, vmin, vmax)
        )

        # A percentile, not the farthest center, so a few strays don't
        # shrink the rest to the middle.
        rmax = 1.3 * np.percentile(to_polar(*points)[1], 95)

        # The fill and the ellipse need the centers to span both axes;
        # a volcano with one or two dates (or all centers on a line)
        # gets neither.
        two_dimensional = (
            len(temp) > 2 and np.linalg.matrix_rank(np.cov(points)) == 2
        )

        # Whatever is drawn first (fill or dots) feeds the colorbar.
        mappable = None
        if fill and two_dimensional:
            kde = gaussian_kde(points)

            # Polar grid, as east/north locations.
            theta, radius = np.meshgrid(
                np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 181), np.linspace(0, rmax, 120)
            )
            grid = np.vstack(
                [
                    (radius * np.sin(theta)).ravel(),
                    (radius * np.cos(theta)).ravel(),
                ]
            )

            # Kernel-weighted mean of the known temperatures at every grid
            # node (Nadaraya-Watson), with the KDE's kernel.
            known = np.isfinite(temp)
            diff = grid[:, :, None] - points[:, None, known]
            inv = np.linalg.inv(kde.covariance)
            kernel = np.exp(
                -0.5 * np.einsum("imn,ij,jmn->mn", diff, inv, diff)
            )
            field = kernel @ temp[known] / kernel.sum(axis=1)

            # Clipped to the color range (no blank cells beyond it), and
            # blanked outside the densest region holding the support share
            # of the centers: its edge is the density that share of the
            # centers reaches.
            edge = np.quantile(kde(points), 1 - self._CENTERS_MAP_SUPPORT)
            field = np.where(
                kde(grid) >= edge, field.clip(norm.vmin, norm.vmax), np.nan
            )
            mappable = ax.contourf(
                theta,
                radius,
                field.reshape(theta.shape),
                levels=MaxNLocator(10).tick_values(norm.vmin, norm.vmax),
                cmap=cmap,
                norm=norm,
            )

        if centers:
            dots = ax.scatter(
                *to_polar(*points),
                c=temp,
                cmap=cmap,
                norm=norm,
                s=18,
                edgecolors="k",  # visible over a fill of its own color
                linewidths=0.5,
                label=f"Centers (n={len(temp)})",
            )
            mappable = dots if mappable is None else mappable

        if spread and two_dimensional:
            # A unit circle stretched along the principal axes of the
            # centers by the standard deviation along each.
            values, vectors = np.linalg.eigh(np.cov(points))
            t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200)
            circle = np.vstack([np.cos(t), np.sin(t)])
            ellipse = vectors @ (np.sqrt(values)[:, None] * circle)
            ax.plot(
                *to_polar(*ellipse),
                color=color,
                linestyle="--",
                label=r"1$\sigma$ spread",
            )

        if reference:
            gvp = to_xy(self._volcano.gvp_lat, self._volcano.gvp_lon)
            ax.scatter(
                *to_polar(*gvp),
                marker="*",
                s=260,
                c=color,
                edgecolors="white",  # the star often lands on dark fill
                zorder=3,
                label="GVP location",
            )

        if colorbar and mappable is not None:
            # Not the ground's temperature: a dot is its own scene's, the
            # fill the mean of the scenes centered nearby.
            ax.figure.colorbar(
                mappable,
                ax=ax,
                pad=0.1,
                shrink=0.8,
                label=f"{temperature} of the scenes centered here",
            )

        _as_compass(ax)
        if rmax > 0:  # a single center leaves nothing to scale to
            ax.set_ylim(0, rmax)
        ax.set_rlabel_position(22.5)  # between N and NE, off the compass
        ax.set_title(
            f"{self._volcano.name}: centers around their centroid (m)"
        )
        if legend:
            ax.legend(
                loc="lower left", bbox_to_anchor=(-0.25, -0.2), frameon=False
            )
        return ax

</content>

#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# License: BSD-3 (https://tldrlegal.com/license/bsd-3-clause-license-(revised))
# Copyright (c) 2026, Rosenfeld, Hernán; Cabral, Juan B.
# All rights reserved.

# =============================================================================
# DOCS
# =============================================================================

"""Accessor base class."""

# =============================================================================
# IMPORTS
# =============================================================================

import abc

# =============================================================================
# ACESSOR ABC
# =============================================================================

# Marks a class attribute as abstract: subclasses that don't override it
# can't be created (see AccessorABC.__init_subclass__).
_ABSTRACT = property(abc.abstractmethod(lambda: ...))


class AccessorABC(abc.ABC):
    """Generalization of the accessor idea for use in volcanicus.

    Instances are callable: the first parameter, ``kind``, names the public
    method to run, and every other argument is passed on to it. Without a
    ``kind`` (or when the first argument isn't a string) the method named by
    the class attribute ``_default_kind`` runs instead, so
    ``volcano.episodes(3.0)`` is ``volcano.episodes.find(3.0)``.

    Every subclass must define ``_default_kind``.

    """

    #: Default method to execute.
    _default_kind = _ABSTRACT

    def __init_subclass__(cls):
        """Validate the creation of a subclass."""
        if cls._default_kind is _ABSTRACT:
            raise TypeError(f"{cls!r} must define a _default_kind")

    def __call__(self, kind=None, *args, **kwargs):
        """x.__call__() <==> x()."""
        if kind is None:
            kind = self._default_kind
        elif not isinstance(kind, str):
            # Not a method name: the first argument of the default method.
            args = (kind, *args)
            kind = self._default_kind

        if kind.startswith("_"):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid kind name '{kind}'")

        method = getattr(self, kind, None)
        if not callable(method):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid kind name '{kind}'")

        return method(*args, **kwargs)

"""Ray view of :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instances \
(``volcano.rays``)."""

# =============================================================================
# IMPORTS
# =============================================================================

import warnings

import numpy as np

import pandas as pd

from ._profiles import (
    distance_radii,
    fill_rays,
    peak_and_efold,
    sector_area,
)
from .base import AccessorABC
from ..constants import (
    DIRECTION_ORDER,
    NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS as _NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS,
    SATURATION_LEVEL,
)

# =============================================================================
# CLASSES
# =============================================================================


class RaysAccessor(AccessorABC):
    """Measurements as rays: one direction of one scene \
    (used as ``volcano.rays``).

    A ray is the radial profile of a single date/direction: one row of the
    source data. Calling the accessor (``volcano.rays()``) is the same as
    :meth:`descriptors`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    volcano : Volcano
        The :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instance this accessor belongs
        to.

    """

    _default_kind = "descriptors"

    def __init__(self, volcano):
        self._volcano = volcano

    def descriptors(self):
        """Summarize every ray (one direction of one scene).

        Describing rays one by one, instead of whole scenes, tells where
        around the vent things happen, and isolates problems that only
        affect one direction.

        - ``peak``: maximum residual along the ray.
        - ``efold_length``: distance (m) from the peak over which the ray
          decays to ``peak / e``; defined exactly as in
          :meth:`DescriptorsAccessor.table`.
        - ``integrated``: residual integrated over the ray's annular
          sector (``2 * pi * r * dr / 8`` per bin), in residual x m². The
          8 rays of a scene add up to its ``integrated``.
        - ``n_saturated``: number of bins at the saturation level
          (:data:`~volcanicus.constants.SATURATION_LEVEL`). Residuals are
          capped there, so a saturated ray's ``peak`` underestimates the
          real anomaly.
        - ``max_abs``: largest absolute residual along the ray, on the raw
          values (see :meth:`flag`).

        Gaps are handled as in :meth:`DescriptorsAccessor.table`. Rays
        missing from the data appear with every descriptor ``NaN``
        (``n_saturated`` 0), so the result always holds 8 rays per scene.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Indexed by ``(date, direction)``, directions in
            :data:`~volcanicus.constants.DIRECTION_ORDER`, with the columns
            ``peak``, ``efold_length``, ``integrated``, ``n_saturated`` and
            ``max_abs``.

        """
        scenes = self._volcano.scenes.grid()
        cube = self._volcano.scenes.grid(as_array=True)
        n_distances = cube.shape[2]
        radii = distance_radii(scenes.columns.unique("distance"))
        filled, interior = fill_rays(cube, radii)

        rays = cube.reshape(-1, n_distances)
        peak, efold_length = peak_and_efold(
            interior.reshape(-1, n_distances), radii
        )
        integrated = (
            filled.reshape(-1, n_distances) * sector_area(radii)
        ).sum(axis=1)
        missing = np.isnan(rays).all(axis=1)
        integrated[missing] = np.nan
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            max_abs = np.nanmax(np.abs(rays), axis=1)

        index = pd.MultiIndex.from_product(
            [scenes.index, DIRECTION_ORDER], names=["date", "direction"]
        )
        return pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "peak": peak,
                "efold_length": efold_length,
                "integrated": integrated,
                "n_saturated": (rays == SATURATION_LEVEL).sum(axis=1),
                "max_abs": max_abs,
            },
            index=index,
        )

    def flag(self, limit=2.0):
        """Flag rays holding a residual too large to be a real measurement.

        Residuals saturate at
        :data:`~volcanicus.constants.SATURATION_LEVEL` (``1.0``), yet a
        handful of rays in the bundled data reach tens or thousands. These
        come in runs along a single direction while the rest of the scene
        looks ordinary, which points to a processing artifact rather than
        to the volcano. The default ``limit`` of twice the saturation level
        keeps the values that only slightly overshoot it.

        Parameters
        ----------
        limit : float, default 2.0
            A ray is flagged when any of its residuals is larger than this
            in absolute value.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.Series
            Boolean, indexed by ``(date, direction)`` like
            :meth:`descriptors`; ``True`` for a flagged ray.

        See Also
        --------
        mask : Drop the flagged rays' values.

        """
        flags = self.descriptors()["max_abs"] > limit
        flags.name = "flagged"
        return flags

    def mask(self, limit=2.0):
        """Blank out every ray :meth:`flag` flags.

        Every distance bin of a flagged ray becomes ``NaN``, so it's
        treated like any other missing ray afterwards (skipped by the
        reductions, fillable by :meth:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano.impute`).
        The whole ray goes, not only the offending values: the bins next to
        an absurd value are rarely trustworthy (in Kadovar a single
        artifact spans 4 bins).

        Parameters
        ----------
        limit : float, default 2.0
            Passed on to :meth:`flag`.

        Returns
        -------
        Volcano
            A new instance with the flagged rays masked. Its metadata
            records the ``mask_limit`` used and how many rays it masked
            (``masked_rays``).

        """
        volcano = self._volcano
        flags = self.flag(limit)
        flagged = flags[flags].index

        df = volcano.to_dataframe()
        distance_columns = [
            c for c in df.columns if c not in _NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS
        ]
        rows = pd.MultiIndex.from_frame(
            df[["date", "direction"]].astype({"direction": str})
        ).isin(flagged)
        df.loc[rows, distance_columns] = np.nan

        metadata = {
            **volcano.metadata,
            "masked_rays": int(rows.sum()),
            "mask_limit": limit,
        }
        # type(volcano) instead of importing Volcano, which imports this
        # module.
        return type(volcano)(
            volcano.name,
            df,
            gvp_lat=volcano.gvp_lat,
            gvp_lon=volcano.gvp_lon,
            metadata=metadata,
        )

</content>

#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# License: BSD-3 (https://tldrlegal.com/license/bsd-3-clause-license-(revised))
# Copyright (c) 2026, Rosenfeld, Hernán; Cabral, Juan B.
# All rights reserved.

# =============================================================================
# DOCS
# =============================================================================

"""Anomaly view of :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instances \
(``volcano.anomalies``)."""

# =============================================================================
# IMPORTS
# =============================================================================

import numpy as np

import pandas as pd

from .base import AccessorABC

# =============================================================================
# CLASSES
# =============================================================================


class AnomaliesAccessor(AccessorABC):
    """Every scene measured against the volcano's usual state \
    (used as ``volcano.anomalies``).

    Calling the accessor (``volcano.anomalies()``) is the same as
    :meth:`zscores`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    volcano : Volcano
        The :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instance this accessor belongs
        to.

    """

    _default_kind = "zscores"

    def __init__(self, volcano):
        self._volcano = volcano

    def baseline(self, min_scenes=10):
        """Typical value and spread of every cell of the scenes.

        For every ``(direction, distance)`` cell, over every scene of this
        volcano: the median (``center``) and a robust spread (``scale``,
        ``1.4826 * MAD``, which matches the standard deviation for normally
        distributed data). Each cell gets its own baseline because each
        direction can sit on a different background (e.g. a slope facing
        the sun, or the sea).

        This is the volcano's *usual* state, not necessarily a quiet one:
        for a volcano active in most of its scenes, "usual" means active,
        and the anomalies (see :meth:`zscores`) measure departures from
        that. Run :meth:`RaysAccessor.mask` first so corrupted rays don't
        leak into it.

        Parameters
        ----------
        min_scenes : int, default 10
            Cells with fewer non-missing scenes than this get a ``NaN``
            baseline: a median and MAD over a handful of values aren't
            meaningful.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Two rows, ``center`` and ``scale``, with the same two-level
            ``(direction, distance)`` columns as
            :meth:`ScenesAccessor.grid`. A cell whose values never vary
            (MAD of 0, e.g. always saturated) has a ``NaN`` scale.

        """
        scenes = self._volcano.scenes.grid()
        center = scenes.median()
        scale = 1.4826 * (scenes - center).abs().median()

        too_few = scenes.count() < min_scenes
        center[too_few] = np.nan
        scale[too_few | (scale == 0)] = np.nan
        return pd.DataFrame({"center": center, "scale": scale}).T

    def zscores(self, min_scenes=10):
        """Every scene as robust z-scores against the volcano's baseline.

        Each cell becomes ``(value - center) / scale``, with ``center`` and
        ``scale`` from :meth:`baseline`: how many "typical deviations" it
        sits above (positive) or below (negative) the volcano's usual value
        for that direction and distance. Unlike raw residuals, these are
        comparable across volcanoes with very different backgrounds.

        Parameters
        ----------
        min_scenes : int, default 10
            Passed on to :meth:`baseline`.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Same shape, index and columns as :meth:`ScenesAccessor.grid`.
            ``NaN`` where the value is missing or the cell has no baseline.

        """
        baseline = self.baseline(min_scenes)
        return (
            self._volcano.scenes.grid() - baseline.loc["center"]
        ) / baseline.loc["scale"]

</content>

<content full_path="accessors/descriptors.py">
#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# License: BSD-3 (https://tldrlegal.com/license/bsd-3-clause-license-(revised))
# Copyright (c) 2026, Rosenfeld, Hernán; Cabral, Juan B.
# All rights reserved.

# =============================================================================
# DOCS
# =============================================================================

"""Descriptors view of :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instances \
(``volcano.descriptors``)."""

# =============================================================================
# IMPORTS
# =============================================================================

import warnings

import numpy as np

import pandas as pd

from ._profiles import (
    distance_radii,
    fill_rays,
    peak_and_efold,
    sector_area,
)
from .base import AccessorABC

# =============================================================================
# CLASSES
# =============================================================================


class DescriptorsAccessor(AccessorABC):
    """Every scene condensed into a few interpretable numbers \
    (used as ``volcano.descriptors``).

    Calling the accessor (``volcano.descriptors()``) is the same as
    :meth:`table`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    volcano : Volcano
        The :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instance this accessor belongs
        to.

    """

    _default_kind = "table"

    def __init__(self, volcano):
        self._volcano = volcano

    def table(self):
        """Summarize every scene with a few interpretable descriptors.

        Each scene (see :meth:`ScenesAccessor.grid`) holds 8 directions x
        every distance bin; this condenses it into five numbers that are
        comparable across dates and volcanoes:

        - ``peak``: maximum of the median (across directions) radial
          profile.
        - ``efold_length``: distance (m) from the peak over which that
          median profile decays to ``peak / e``, the crossing linearly
          interpolated between bins. Measured from the peak (not from the
          vent) so it doesn't depend on which inner bins a scene happens to
          have: for an exponential decay it's the decay length whatever
          the first bin is. ``NaN`` if the peak isn't positive or the
          profile never drops that far within the measured distances.
        - ``integrated``: the residual integrated over the whole disk, each
          bin weighted by the area of its annular sector
          (``2 * pi * r * dr / 8``), in residual x m². A missing direction
          is skipped and the rest are scaled up to the full disk.
        - ``anisotropy``: how concentrated the heat is in one direction, in
          ``[0, 1]``: ``0`` spreads evenly around the vent, ``1`` sits
          entirely in a single direction. It's the length of the vector sum
          of the 8 directions, each as long as its ray's positive ``peak``
          (see :meth:`RaysAccessor.descriptors`), over the sum of their
          lengths. Using the ray peaks keeps it about the near field:
          weighting by area instead would let the far field, which covers
          most of the disk, decide the direction.
        - ``azimuth``: direction of that vector sum, in degrees clockwise
          from north (``N`` is 0, ``E`` is 90, ``S`` is 180, ``O`` is 270).
          ``NaN`` when no direction dominates (``anisotropy`` is 0).

        ``anisotropy`` and ``azimuth`` need all 8 directions, so they're
        ``NaN`` for a scene with a direction missing entirely (see
        :meth:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano.impute` to fill those first).

        Gaps along a direction are filled by linear interpolation over
        distance before computing anything; otherwise a bin missing in some
        scenes and not in others would make descriptors incomparable
        between scenes. For the integrals, the edges also take the nearest
        available bin (the innermost one is often missing, and leaving it
        out would undercount). ``peak`` and ``efold_length`` don't
        extrapolate, so a scene missing its innermost bin peaks at the
        first bin it has.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Indexed by ``date``, with the columns ``peak``,
            ``efold_length``, ``integrated``, ``anisotropy`` and
            ``azimuth``.

        See Also
        --------
        RaysAccessor.descriptors : The same kind of descriptors, per
            direction.

        """
        scenes = self._volcano.scenes.grid()
        cube = self._volcano.scenes.grid(as_array=True)
        n_dates, n_directions, n_distances = cube.shape
        radii = distance_radii(scenes.columns.unique("distance"))
        filled, interior = fill_rays(cube, radii)
        missing_direction = np.isnan(cube).all(axis=2)

        # peak & efold_length: shape of the typical (median) profile.
        # A bin with no data in any direction is an expected NaN, not
        # something to warn about.
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            median_profile = np.nanmedian(interior, axis=1)
        peak, efold_length = peak_and_efold(median_profile, radii)

        # integrated: per-direction integrals; a missing direction is
        # skipped and the mean of the others stands in for it.
        direction_integral = (filled * sector_area(radii)).sum(axis=2)
        direction_integral[missing_direction] = np.nan
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            integrated = np.nanmean(direction_integral, axis=1) * n_directions

        # anisotropy & azimuth: vector sum of every ray's positive peak,
        # each pointing along its compass bearing.
        ray_peak, _ = peak_and_efold(interior.reshape(-1, n_distances), radii)
        positive = np.clip(ray_peak.reshape(n_dates, n_directions), 0, None)
        bearings = np.radians(45.0 * np.arange(n_directions))
        east = (positive * np.sin(bearings)).sum(axis=1)
        north = (positive * np.cos(bearings)).sum(axis=1)
        total = positive.sum(axis=1)
        with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
            anisotropy = np.hypot(east, north) / total
        # A perfectly even scene leaves floating-point crumbs in the vector
        # sum; snap those to 0 so they don't fake a bearing.
        anisotropy[np.isclose(anisotropy, 0, atol=1e-9)] = 0
        azimuth = np.degrees(np.arctan2(east, north)) % 360
        undefined = missing_direction.any(axis=1) | ~(total > 0)
        anisotropy[undefined] = np.nan
        azimuth[undefined | (anisotropy == 0)] = np.nan

        return pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "peak": peak,
                "efold_length": efold_length,
                "integrated": integrated,
                "anisotropy": anisotropy,
                "azimuth": azimuth,
            },
            index=scenes.index,
        )

</content>

#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# License: BSD-3 (https://tldrlegal.com/license/bsd-3-clause-license-(revised))
# Copyright (c) 2026, Rosenfeld, Hernán; Cabral, Juan B.
# All rights reserved.

# =============================================================================
# DOCS
# =============================================================================

"""Statistics accessor for :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instances \
(``volcano.stats``)."""

# =============================================================================
# IMPORTS
# =============================================================================

from .base import AccessorABC
from ..constants import (
    GROUPBY_WHITELIST,
    NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS as _NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS,
)

# =============================================================================
# CLASSES
# =============================================================================


class StatsAccessor(AccessorABC):
    """Calculate basic statistics of the volcano measurements \
    (used as ``volcano.stats``).

    Kind of statistic to produce:

    - 'cov' : Compute pairwise covariance of distance-bin columns,
      excluding NA/null values.
    - 'describe' : Generate descriptive statistics.
    - 'kurtosis' : Return unbiased kurtosis over requested axis.
    - 'max' : Return the maximum of the values over the requested axis.
    - 'mean' : Return the mean of the values over the requested axis.
    - 'median' : Return the median of the values over the requested
      axis.
    - 'min' : Return the minimum of the values over the requested axis.
    - 'pct_change' : Percentage change between the current and a prior
      element.
    - 'quantile' : Return values at the given quantile over requested
      axis.
    - 'sem' : Return unbiased standard error of the mean over requested
      axis.
    - 'skew' : Return unbiased skew over requested axis.
    - 'std' : Return sample standard deviation over requested axis.
    - 'var' : Return unbiased variance over requested axis.

    Every statistic is computed per group: the mandatory first parameter
    ``groupby`` (either ``"date"`` or ``"direction"``) selects which column
    to group the measurements by before the underlying pandas method is
    applied.

    Parameters
    ----------
    volcano : Volcano
        The :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instance this accessor belongs
        to.

    """

    # The list of methods that can be accessed of the subjacent dataframe.
    _DF_WHITELIST = (
        "cov",
        "describe",
        "kurtosis",
        "max",
        "mean",
        "median",
        "min",
        "pct_change",
        "quantile",
        "sem",
        "skew",
        "std",
        "var",
    )
    _default_kind = "describe"

    def __init__(self, volcano):
        self._volcano = volcano

    def _grouped(self, groupby):
        """Distance-bin columns of the volcano's DataFrame, grouped."""
        # Reject anything but "date"/"direction" up front, before doing any
        # work, so every stat method gets the same clear error for free.
        if groupby not in GROUPBY_WHITELIST:
            raise ValueError(
                f"'groupby' must be one of {GROUPBY_WHITELIST}, "
                f"found {groupby!r}"
            )
        df = self._volcano.to_dataframe()
        distance_columns = [
            c for c in df.columns if c not in _NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS
        ]
        # Pre-select the distance columns so callers' pandas method calls
        # (mean, describe, ...) never see date/direction/lat/long.
        return df.groupby(groupby, observed=True)[distance_columns]

    def __getattr__(self, a):
        """x.__getattr__(a) <==> x.a <==> getattr(x, "a")."""
        if a not in self._DF_WHITELIST:
            raise AttributeError(a)

        def method(groupby, **kwargs):
            grouped = self._grouped(groupby)
            return grouped.apply(lambda g: getattr(g, a)(**kwargs))

        return method

    def __dir__(self):
        """x.__dir__() <==> dir(x)."""
        return super().__dir__() + list(self._DF_WHITELIST)

</content>

<content full_path="accessors/scenes.py">
#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# License: BSD-3 (https://tldrlegal.com/license/bsd-3-clause-license-(revised))
# Copyright (c) 2026, Rosenfeld, Hernán; Cabral, Juan B.
# All rights reserved.

# =============================================================================
# DOCS
# =============================================================================

"""Scene view of :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instances \
(``volcano.scenes``)."""

# =============================================================================
# IMPORTS
# =============================================================================

import pandas as pd

from .base import AccessorABC
from ..constants import (
    DIRECTION_ORDER,
    NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS as _NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS,
    REDUCE_DIRECTIONS_WHITELIST,
)

# =============================================================================
# CLASSES
# =============================================================================


class ScenesAccessor(AccessorABC):
    """Measurements as scenes: one row per date (used as ``volcano.scenes``).

    A scene is everything observed on a single date: a grid of every
    direction x every distance bin. Calling the accessor
    (``volcano.scenes()``) is the same as :meth:`grid`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    volcano : Volcano
        The :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` instance this accessor belongs
        to.

    """

    _default_kind = "grid"

    def __init__(self, volcano):
        self._volcano = volcano

    def grid(self, as_array=False):
        """Reshape the measurements into one scene (date) per row.

        The source DataFrame is "long" on direction (one row per
        date/direction). Each scene becomes a single row, which is the
        natural sample unit for a model.

        The grid is always complete: directions follow
        :data:`~volcanicus.constants.DIRECTION_ORDER` and any date/direction
        pair absent from the source data is filled with ``NaN``, so every
        scene has exactly the same shape (and the same columns) no matter
        the volcano.

        Parameters
        ----------
        as_array : bool, default False
            If False, return a DataFrame. If True, return the same values as
            a 3-D ``numpy.ndarray`` of shape
            ``(n_dates, n_directions, n_distances)``.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame or numpy.ndarray
            DataFrame indexed by ``date``, with two-level columns
            ``(direction, distance)``; or its values as a cube (see
            ``as_array``). In the cube, axis 0 follows the sorted dates,
            axis 1 follows ``DIRECTION_ORDER`` and axis 2 the distance bins
            in their original (increasing) order.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the data can't be laid out as a grid of scenes: a direction
            not in ``DIRECTION_ORDER`` (it would be silently dropped), a
            date that failed to parse (``NaT``) or a repeated
            date/direction pair.

        """
        df = self._volcano.to_dataframe()

        # The grid below is reindexed to DIRECTION_ORDER, which would
        # silently turn a misspelled direction into NaN; fail loudly instead.
        unknown = set(df["direction"].astype(str)) - set(DIRECTION_ORDER)
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unknown direction(s) {sorted(unknown)}; "
                f"expected values in {DIRECTION_ORDER}"
            )
        # normalize_dataframe coerces unparseable dates to NaT, which would
        # otherwise end up as a scene with no date.
        if df["date"].isna().any():
            raise ValueError(
                f"{df['date'].isna().sum()} row(s) have an invalid date (NaT)"
            )
        duplicated = df.duplicated(["date", "direction"])
        if duplicated.any():
            pairs = df.loc[duplicated, ["date", "direction"]]
            raise ValueError(
                "Repeated date/direction pair(s): "
                f"{list(pairs.itertuples(index=False, name=None))}"
            )

        distance_columns = [
            c for c in df.columns if c not in _NON_DISTANCE_COLUMNS
        ]
        # (date, direction) -> one row; then direction moves from the rows
        # into the columns, next to the distance bins.
        wide = df.set_index(["date", "direction"])[distance_columns].unstack(
            "direction"
        )

        # unstack leaves (distance, direction) columns in arbitrary order and
        # only for the directions present; force the full, canonical grid so
        # every volcano yields identically shaped scenes.
        full_columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_product(
            [DIRECTION_ORDER, distance_columns],
            names=["direction", "distance"],
        )
        scenes = (
            wide.swaplevel(axis=1).reindex(columns=full_columns).sort_index()
        )

        if as_array:
            return scenes.to_numpy(dtype=float).reshape(
                len(scenes), len(DIRECTION_ORDER), len(distance_columns)
            )
        return scenes

    def reduce(self, how="median"):
        """Collapse the directions of every scene into a single profile.

        Each scene (see :meth:`grid`) holds 8 directions x every distance
        bin; this reduces the 8 directions at each distance with ``how``,
        leaving one radial profile per date.

        ``NaN`` values are skipped while reducing, so a missing direction
        doesn't spoil the others; a distance bin where every direction is
        missing stays ``NaN``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        how : str, default "median"
            Reduction to apply across directions: one of ``"count"``,
            ``"max"``, ``"mean"``, ``"median"``, ``"min"``, ``"std"``,
            ``"sum"`` or ``"var"``.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Indexed by ``date``, with one column per distance bin.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``how`` is not a supported reduction.

        See Also
        --------
        median : Shorthand for ``reduce("median")``.
        max : Shorthand for ``reduce("max")``.

        """
        if how not in REDUCE_DIRECTIONS_WHITELIST:
            raise ValueError(
                f"'how' must be one of {REDUCE_DIRECTIONS_WHITELIST}, "
                f"found {how!r}"
            )
        # Transpose so every (direction, distance) pair is a row, then group
        # those rows by distance: each group holds the 8 directions to reduce.
        by_distance = self.grid().T.groupby(level="distance", sort=False)
        reduced = getattr(by_distance, how)().T
        reduced.columns.name = "distance"
        return reduced

    def median(self):
        """Typical radial profile of every scene: median across directions.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Indexed by ``date``, with one column per distance bin. Using the
            median (not the mean) keeps a single anomalous direction from
            dragging the profile.

        See Also
        --------
        grid : The full, per-direction scenes this is reduced from.
        max : Hottest direction of every scene.

        """
        return self.reduce("median")

    def max(self):  # noqa: A003
        """Hottest direction of every scene: maximum across directions.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Indexed by ``date``, with one column per distance bin.

        See Also
        --------
        grid : The full, per-direction scenes this is reduced from.
        median : Typical (median) profile of every scene.

        """
        return self.reduce("max")

</content>

<content full_path="datasets/__init__.py">
#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# License: BSD-3 (https://tldrlegal.com/license/bsd-3-clause-license-(revised))
# Copyright (c) 2026, Rosenfeld, Hernán; Cabral, Juan B.
# All rights reserved.

# =============================================================================
# DOCS
# =============================================================================

"""The :mod:`volcanicus.datasets` module includes utilities to load \
bundled example :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` datasets.

Each dataset lives in its own directory, ``<name>/``, holding the
measurements (``<name>.csv``) and the volcano's descriptive metadata
(``<name>.json``).

"""

# =============================================================================
# IMPORTS
# =============================================================================

import functools
import json
import os
import pathlib

import pandas as pd

from ..core import Volcano

# =============================================================================
# CONSTANTS
# =============================================================================

_PATH = pathlib.Path(os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(__file__)))

# =============================================================================
# FUNCTIONS
# =============================================================================


@functools.cache
def available() -> list[str]:
    """List the volcano names bundled with :mod:`volcanicus.datasets`.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        Names accepted by :func:`load`, sorted alphabetically.

    """
    return sorted(
        p.parts[-2]
        for p in _PATH.glob("*/*.csv")
        if not p.parts[-2].startswith(".")
    )


def load(volcano_name):
    """Load a bundled example :class:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano` dataset.

    Parameters
    ----------
    volcano_name : str
        Name of the bundled volcano to load (see :func:`available` for the
        valid values). Matched case-sensitively against the dataset
        directory name.

    Returns
    -------
    Volcano
        A new instance built from the bundled ``<name>.csv`` measurements,
        with the ``latitude``/``longitude`` of ``<name>.json`` as its GVP
        reference location (:attr:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano.gvp_lat`,
        :attr:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano.gvp_lon`) and the rest of the file
        as its :attr:`~volcanicus.core.Volcano.metadata`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``volcano_name`` is not a bundled dataset.

    """
    data_path = _PATH / volcano_name / f"{volcano_name}.csv"
    metadata_path = _PATH / volcano_name / f"{volcano_name}.json"
    if not data_path.exists():
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown volcano {volcano_name!r}")

    data = pd.read_csv(data_path)
    metadata = json.loads(metadata_path.read_text())
    gvp_lat = metadata.pop("latitude")
    gvp_lon = metadata.pop("longitude")

    return Volcano(
        name=volcano_name,
        df=data,
        gvp_lat=gvp_lat,
        gvp_lon=gvp_lon,
        metadata=metadata,
    )

</content>

#!/usr/bin/env python
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# License: BSD-3 (https://tldrlegal.com/license/bsd-3-clause-license-(revised))
# Copyright (c) 2026, Rosenfeld, Hernán; Cabral, Juan B.
# All rights reserved.

# =============================================================================
# DOCS
# =============================================================================

"""Container object exposing keys as attributes."""

# =============================================================================
# IMPORTS
# =============================================================================

import copy
from collections.abc import Mapping

# =============================================================================
# BUNCH
# =============================================================================


class Bunch(Mapping):
    """Container object exposing keys as attributes.

    Concept based on the sklearn.utils.Bunch.

    Bunch objects are sometimes used as an output for functions and methods.
    They extend dictionaries by enabling values to be accessed by key,
    `bunch["value_key"]`, or by an attribute, `bunch.value_key`.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> b = Bunch("data", {"a": 1, "b": 2})
    >>> b
    data({a, b})
    >>> b['b']
    2
    >>> b.b
    2

    """

    def __init__(self, name, data):
        if not isinstance(data, Mapping):
            raise TypeError("Data must be some kind of mapping")
        super().__setattr__("_name", str(name))
        super().__setattr__("_data", data)

    def __getitem__(self, k):
        """x.__getitem__(y) <==> x[y]."""
        return self._data[k]

    def __getattr__(self, a):
        """x.__getattr__(y) <==> x.y."""
        try:
            return self._data[a]
        except KeyError:
            raise AttributeError(a)

    def __setattr__(self, a, v):
        """x.__setattr__(a, v) <==> x.a = v."""
        raise AttributeError(f"Bunch {self._name!r} is read-only")

    def __copy__(self):
        """x.__copy__() <==> copy.copy(x)."""
        cls = type(self)
        return cls(str(self._name), data=self._data)

    def __deepcopy__(self, memo):
        """x.__deepcopy__() <==> copy.copy(x)."""
        # extract the class
        cls = type(self)

        # make the copy but without the data
        clone = cls(name=str(self._name), data={})

        # store in the memo that clone is copy of self
        # https://docs.python.org/3/library/copy.html
        memo[id(self)] = clone

        # now we copy the data
        super(cls, clone).__setattr__("_data", copy.deepcopy(self._data, memo))

        return clone

    def __iter__(self):
        """x.__iter__() <==> iter(x)."""
        return iter(self._data)

    def __len__(self):
        """x.__len__() <==> len(x)."""
        return len(self._data)

    def __repr__(self):
        """x.__repr__() <==> repr(x)."""
        content = repr(set(self._data)) if self._data else "{}"
        return f"<{self._name} {content}>"

    def __dir__(self):
        """x.__dir__() <==> dir(x)."""
        return super().__dir__() + list(self._data)

    def __setstate__(self, state):
        """Needed for multiprocessing environment."""
        self.__dict__.update(state)

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        """Get item from bunch."""
        return self._data.get(key, default)

    def to_dict(self):
        """Convert the Bunch object to a dictionary.

        This method performs a deep copy of the _data attribute, ensuring
        that the original data remains unchanged.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            A deep copy of the _data attribute.

        Example
        -------
        >>> bunch = Bunch("data", {"key1": "value1", "key2": "value2"})
        >>> dict_data = bunch.to_dict()
        >>> print(dict_data)
        {'key1': 'value1', 'key2': 'value2'}

        """
        return copy.deepcopy(self._data)

</content>
